mcp.title: Connect an agent
mcp.intro: An agent such as a desktop assistant or a coding tool can read and write in Scríobh through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), using one of your API keys. This page gives the address and the configuration to paste into the agent's settings.
mcp.off: The MCP endpoint is switched off on this server (SCRIOBH_MCP=off). No agent can connect over MCP until the administrator switches it on.
mcp.on: The MCP endpoint is on. It offers {n} tools in all; a key sees only those its scope and restriction allow.
mcp.addr_note: The address is this server's own, as your browser reached it, with the choices below in its query. The agent sends your key with every request; there is no sign-in.
mcp.set_core: The manuscript: projects, documents, the outline, search, comments, suggestions, revisions, review, goals and statistics
mcp.set_bible: The bible: Compendiums, entities, the timeline, mentions and scenes
mcp.set_all: Every tool (about 200: more than most agents handle well)
mcp.readonly_hint: The agent sees only tools that cannot change anything, even with a key that can write. Leave it on until you trust what the agent does.
mcp.config_note: Replace scr_… with a key. The shapes below follow each program's own documentation as it was read when this page was written; they were not run against those programs here, so check the program's own page if one is refused.
mcp.sn_desktop_note: Paste into the client's MCP settings file. It starts the scriobh-cli command, which talks to this server for the agent.
mcp.sn_cli_note: The same proxy, started by hand or by any client that runs a command. It needs scriobh-cli installed; after scriobh-cli login the two variables can be left out.
mcp.sn_remote_note: For a client that connects to an address itself and can send a header. A client that can only sign in with OAuth cannot use this endpoint.
mcp.sn_opencode_note: Under mcp in opencode.json. OpenCode can also run the command above, as type local.
mcp.keys_what: Any live API key of yours works; what the agent can do is what the key allows, and every call is checked again as if you had made it.
mcp.keys_read: A read-only key sees only the tools that read.
mcp.keys_write: A read and write key adds the tools that change things. Deleting moves things to the trash, except for a few tools that destroy for good: those are offered only when the administrator allowed them and the address asks for them.
mcp.keys_pin: A key restricted to one project sees only that project and the Compendiums it uses; nothing else on the server exists for it. Give an agent a key restricted to the project it works on.
mcp.keys_cookie: A browser sign-in never works here: the endpoint reads a key and nothing else.
mcp.keys_cannot: Your account cannot hold API keys on this server: ask an administrator.
mcp.groups_note: Each group is one part of the application. Name the groups an agent needs: a long list of tools costs the agent attention and room.
mcp.perm_on: Tools that destroy for good are allowed on this server, for a key that can write and an address that asks for them with permanent=1.
mcp.perm_off: Tools that destroy for good are not offered on this server.
mcp.admin_on: Membership tools are offered to an administration key.
mcp.never_keys: API keys, browser sessions, preferences and your profile.
mcp.never_share: Share links and webhooks: sending the book or its news to an address is your decision.
mcp.never_git: Git remotes and pushes, backups and the mirror.
mcp.never_ai: The writing assistant's recipes: an agent brings its own model.
mcp.never_contact: The manuscript's contact block (name, address, email, phone), and the compiled files whose title page carries it.
mcp.never_purge: Deleting a whole project or Compendium for good.
mcp.never_cred: Anything that takes a password, token or other credential.
mcp.data_note: Everything an agent reads from a project is your writing, and every tool says so: it is data for the agent, never instructions. Keep write keys narrow.
wh.title: Webhooks
wh.intro: A webhook sends a short, signed notice to an address you choose when something happens in this project: a document saved (ids and word counts), a comment or a suggestion made (ids), an export finished. The words of the book never go with it.
wh.owner_only: Only the owner of a project sets up its webhooks.
wh.off: Webhooks are switched off on this server.
wh.once_note: Copy it now and store it where the receiver can read it. It is shown this once and never again; if it is lost, rotate it.
wh.verify_h: How the receiver checks a notice
wh.verify: Every notice carries a timestamp and a signature. The receiver computes the signature with the secret and refuses a notice whose signature differs or whose timestamp is more than five minutes off. A notice may arrive twice: keep the ids you have seen and apply each once.
wh.verify_code:
Scriobh-Webhook-Timestamp: <unix seconds>
Scriobh-Webhook-Signature: v1=hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + body))
Scriobh-Webhook-Id: <the same on every attempt>
wh.queue: Waiting to be sent: {pending}. Failed for good: {dead}.
wh.path_sealed: (the rest of the address is kept sealed and never shown)
wh.m_streak: {n} failed in a row; at 10 it is switched off
wh.test_ok: The test was delivered: the receiver answered {status}.
wh.test_soon: A test was sent a moment ago. Wait five seconds and try again.
wh.now_off: The webhook is off. What was waiting for it was dropped.
wh.now_on: The webhook is on. It hears of what happens from now on, not of what it missed.
wh.edit: Change, rotate the secret or delete
wh.name: Name
wh.name_hint: What it is for, so you know it again.
wh.new_url_hint: Leave empty to keep the current one. A new address replaces the whole of the old one.
wh.keep_hint: 0 to 168. During this time every notice is signed with both secrets, so the receiver can change over without a gap.
wh.keep_number: Write the hours as a whole number from 0 to 168.
wh.rotate_ask: Make a new signing secret? It is shown once, on the next page.
wh.delete_ask: Delete {name} and its delivery log? Notices still waiting are dropped. This cannot be undone.
wh.delete_note: Its delivery log and anything waiting go with it.
wh.log_note: Newest first. A notice that fails is tried again after 10 seconds, a minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2, 6, 12 and 24 hours, then it has failed for good. A refusal (a 4xx) or a redirect ends it at once. No log holds what was sent or the receiver's answer, only a few cleaned words of a failure.
wh.requeued: The notice is queued again, with the same id.
wh.url_rules: Starts with https://. No user name or password in it. The server refuses addresses inside a private network, the machine itself and cloud metadata addresses, however they are written, and checks again each time it connects; redirects are never followed.
wh.url_private_on: This server allows addresses on its own machine and network, and plain http to those.
wh.url_private_off: This server does not send to local or private addresses.
wh.url_sealed: Only the scheme, host and port are shown again; the rest of the address is kept sealed, so a receiver's token in it stays private.
wh.text_warn: With this on, every new comment's words (up to 2,000 characters) leave this server with the notice. Leave it off unless the receiver needs them.
wh.never: Nothing else a webhook sends ever carries text: no document, title, name, note, research or Compendium entry.
wh.ev_document.updated: A document was saved: its id, revision and word count.
wh.ev_comment.created: A comment was made: its id, its thread and document.
wh.ev_suggestion.created: A suggestion was made: its id and document.
wh.ev_export.completed: An export finished: its id, format, documents and size.
wh.err_blocked: The address was refused by the network guard.
wh.err_redirect_refused: The receiver answered with a redirect, which is never followed.
wh.err_rate_limited: The receiver asked to slow down.
wh.err_gone: The receiver asked not to be called again.
wh.err_secret: The signing secret could not be opened: rotate it.

site.where_note: Inside the server's sites folder. The administrator points the web server there.
site.where_none: Not published yet; the folder is made by the first publish.
site.no_base: None set: no feeds, sitemap or canonical links.
site.no_publish: Publishing to a folder is not set up on this server (the administrator has not chosen a folder). You can still download the site as a zip and put it on any web host.
site.publish_ask: Publish the site now to a new folder in the server's sites folder?
site.publish_ask_replace: Publish the site now? It replaces what is in {where}.
site.overwrite: Replace the files that were changed by hand
site.explicit: Nothing is published by itself: only this button publishes.
site.warn_note: None of these stops a publish.
site.pages_none: No pages. Front and back matter become pages; a post can be made one.
site.out_note: Documents that are not published, and why. Only done documents are published unless drafts are included.
site.date_created: the date it was made: set one
site.d_slug_hint: Letters, digits and hyphens. Empty: made from the title. An address that has been published stays with its document.
site.d_unpin: Let the address {slug} be made again
site.d_excerpt_hint: Up to 300 characters, shown in lists and feeds. Empty: the first paragraph.
site.opt_note: Only what you change is saved. Nothing is published by saving.

site.o_base_hint: For example https://example.org/blog/. With it the site gets RSS and Atom feeds, a sitemap and canonical links; without it they are left out.
site.o_lang_hint: A tag such as en or ga-IE. Empty: the project's.
site.o_posts_chapters: Every chapter (its scenes are folded in)
site.o_drafts: Also publish drafts and documents marked revise
site.o_parts: A post in a part is in a category named after the part
site.o_cover: The project's cover on the front page
site.o_accent_hint: Each is shown in its light and dark form, and checked for readable contrast in both.
site.o_about_hint: A page of the site: the author's name links to it and it comes first in the navigation.
site.o_nav_hint: Up to 8, shown in the navigation. Empty rows are ignored.
site.o_noindex_hint: Asks search engines to stay away: every page says noindex and robots.txt disallows everything.
site.o_reset_ask: Put every site option back to its default?
site.o_reset_done: Every option is back to its default.
site.w_image_missing: A picture that cannot be published
site.status_fix: Change its status in the outline.
site.pinned_kept: It keeps the address {slug} from an earlier publish, so no other document can take it.

mail.settings.title: Email
mail.settings.intro: Nothing is sent until an administrator switches mail on. When it is on, this server sends only what a person asked for: a delivery to their own Kindle, a digest they turned on. It never sends manuscript text in a digest, and it sends nothing to anyone who did not ask.
mail.settings.security_starttls: STARTTLS (port 587): upgraded before anything is sent
mail.settings.security_none: None: only for a relay on this machine, never with a password
mail.settings.allow_private: The relay is on this machine or my own network

editions.diff.current: This project as it is now
editions.diff.source_record: Read from the text kept when the book was imported
editions.diff.match.recorded: Recorded when the book was imported
editions.diff.match.title: Same title
editions.diff.summary: {edited} edited, {added} added, {removed} removed, {moved} moved, {split} split, {merged} merged, {unchanged} unchanged
editions.diff.taken: The chapter is the edition's again. The text it had before is saved in the chapter's history.
editions.diff.too_different: These two texts have too little in common to compare chapter by chapter.
editions.diff.partial: The comparison was cut short: some chapters differ but were not compared word by word.
editions.diff.text_for_editors: The text of an edition is for the project's editors.
editions.diff.confirm_guess: These chapters were paired by comparing them, not from a record. Check that this is the chapter you mean, then take it.

imp.js.too_big: That file is larger than 32 MiB, which is the most that can be sent or kept.

imp.js.busy: The server is busy with other imports. Nothing was imported and your file is still chosen. Try again in a moment.
imp.js.map_help: This is how the book becomes parts, chapters and front and back matter. Open Edit on a line to rename it, change what it is, nest it under a part or a chapter, join it to another, or leave it out. Move up and Move down put it in order. Nothing is created until you press the button at the end.
imp.js.cut_toc: By the book's table of contents{from}
imp.js.cut_files: One chapter for each file of the book
imp.js.cover_none: This book has no cover picture.
imp.js.cover_kept: The cover picture is kept as an attachment of the project.
imp.js.cover_not: The cover picture was not kept: {reason}
imp.js.label: Name of this edition
imp.js.label_hint: The title and the year unless you say otherwise. The original file is kept on this server, as it was received, under this name, and you can download it from Editions. It is not in the Markdown copy, it is never pushed to Git, and it is shared with no one.
imp.js.files_h: The book's files and what each became ({n})
imp.js.files_more: And {n} more files, not listed here.
imp.js.pdf_h: What was read from the PDF
imp.js.pdf_headings: proposed from headings set larger than the text
imp.js.pdf_lost_h: What could and could not be recovered
imp.js.pdf_tables: Tables: rows flattened to one paragraph each, cells separated by |: {n}, on pages {p}. A PDF's tables are not rebuilt.
imp.js.pdf_images: Pictures on the pages, not imported: {n}. The text around them was imported.
imp.js.pdf_links: Links, underline, colour and type size: not kept. The text of a link stays.
imp.js.pdf_cols: Columns: pages read as two columns, left then right: {n}. Pages that may have columns or a table, read as one column: {p}.
imp.js.pdf_cols0: Columns: every page was read as one column. Three or more columns are not read as columns.
imp.js.pdf_scan: Scanned pages, left out because they are pictures with no text: {n}. No character recognition is done, and none is promised.
imp.js.pdf_scan0: Scanned pages: none. Every page has a text layer.
imp.js.pdf_rtl: Right-to-left text on pages {p} is kept in the order the file stores it, which is not always the reading order.
imp.js.pdf_unmapped: Characters with no known meaning, left out: {n}.
imp.js.pdf_cut: A limit was reached on pages {p}: part of them was not read.
imp.js.pdf_heads: Running head and page number lines removed: {n}. The rule: {rule}
imp.js.pdf_pages_h: Pages worth a look ({n}, least reliable first)
imp.js.pdf_nokeep: The PDF itself is not kept. Only its checksum is recorded with the import.
imp.js.tr_ins: In whole paragraphs a reviewer inserted (the text is kept): {n}.
imp.js.tr_del: In whole paragraphs a reviewer deleted (that text is not kept): {n}.
imp.js.tr_cap: Over the limits for suggestions (300 a document, 1,000 an import): {n}.
imp.js.tr_place: Not found in the text exactly once: {n}.
imp.js.tr_refused: That the review checks would not allow: {n}.
imp.js.tr_conflict: Too close to a change by another author: {n}.
imp.js.tr_edge: At the edge of bold or italic text: {n}.
imp.js.tr_suggest: The chapters hold the original text, as its author left it. Each change a reviewer made waits as a suggestion, which you accept or reject in Review under the reviewer's Word name. Accepting them all gives the reviewers' text.
imp.js.tr_accept: The chapters hold the final text, with every change accepted. No suggestions are written.
imp.js.tr_reject: The chapters hold the original text, with every change rejected. No suggestions are written.
imp.js.tr_rule: Where two reviewers changed the same sentence, the later change is already in the text and is not a suggestion. A whole paragraph a reviewer deleted is gone from the text, and a whole paragraph one inserted is in it.
imp.js.tr_comments: Word comments to be written as comments: {n}.
imp.js.tr_comments_lost: Word comments not imported (in a heading, a table or a footnote, or over the limit): {n}.
imp.js.tr_taken: Changes that cannot be suggestions and are taken as the reviewer left them: {n}
imp.js.tr_pairs: Reviewers whose changes met, the later one's change is in the text: {pairs}.
imp.js.tr_moves: Tracked moves, each now a deletion and an insertion: {n}.
imp.js.top: The top level of the book
imp.js.join_note: Its text is added to the end of the one you choose, and this one is removed. Footnotes are renumbered so none collide. You can undo this under Left out of the import.
imp.js.done_edn: Kept the original file as edition “{label}”. You can download it from Editions.
imp.js.done_edn_plain: Kept the original file as an edition. You can download it from Editions.
imp.js.done_sug: Suggestions waiting in Review, under the reviewers' Word names: {n}. The chapters hold the original text until you accept them.
imp.fmt_pdf: A PDF with a text layer
imp.dc_suggest_d: The chapters keep the original text, and each change a reviewer made waits as a suggestion for you to accept or reject. This is the usual choice.
imp.dc_accept_d: The chapters hold the final text, with every change taken in. Nothing waits for review.
imp.dc_reject_d: The chapters hold the original text, with every change thrown away. Nothing waits for review.
imp.dc_note: Word comments are imported as comments in every case, under their authors' Word names. With suggestions, where two reviewers changed the same sentence the later change is already in the text and is not a suggestion, and a whole paragraph a reviewer deleted is gone from the text. The preview counts each of these.
imp.epub_into: The book's chapters are added to this project as new chapters after what is already there. Nothing that is there now is changed. The original file is kept as an edition of this project.
imp.epub_new: The book becomes a new project. To add a book to a project you already have, open that project's menu and choose Add files from a folder or zip.
imp.epub_hint: Version 2 or 3, up to {mb} MB. Books with copy protection (DRM), fixed-layout books and files that are not books are refused, and the preview says why. The book is read on this server. Nothing in it is run or fetched.
imp.es_h: How to cut the book into chapters
imp.es_auto_d: It uses the table of contents when the book has a usable one, then the book's files, then its headings. The preview says which it used.
imp.es_toc_d: Each entry starts a chapter, and the nesting of the contents becomes parts and chapters.
imp.es_files_d: One chapter for each file in the book's reading order. Good for books made by splitting a manuscript into files.
imp.es_headings_d: A new chapter at each chapter-level heading. Good for a book that is one long file.
imp.ep_h: The cover page and the title page
imp.ep_skip_d: The project's own title and author replace them. The cover picture is kept as an attachment.
imp.ep_keep_d: It is imported as front matter. A contents page is always left out, because a contents is made when the book is compiled.
imp.epub_again: Choosing another cut starts the chapters again, and any changes you made to them are dropped.
imp.epub_safe: The cuts are a proposal. Nothing is created until you have looked at the chapters and pressed the button at the end.
imp.pdf_hint: Up to {mb} MB, with a text layer. Chapters come from the PDF's outline, or from headings set larger than the text. Running heads, page numbers and a contents page are removed.
imp.pdf_isolated: The PDF is read in a separate process on this server, with a time limit and a memory limit. A file that is too complex or damaged may be refused, and the preview then says so. Nothing in a PDF is run.
imp.pdf_refused: Scanned PDFs, whose pages are pictures, are refused: Scríobh reads the text a PDF carries and does no character recognition. Password-protected PDFs are refused, and no password is tried.
imp.pdf_lost: A PDF does not say where its paragraphs, tables and links are, so the reading is a best guess. The preview lists what could not be recovered, and a confidence for the pages least likely to be right. The PDF itself is not kept.
editions.detail_intro: The book as it was imported, and the chapters it was read as.
editions.empty_hint: When you import an EPUB book into this project, the file is kept here as it was received, with its checksum and the chapters it was read as.
editions.empty_link: Add a book to this project
editions.by_gone: Someone who is no longer on the project
editions.no_file_short: The original file is not on this server.
editions.keep_a: The original file is kept on this server only. It is not in the Markdown copy, it is never pushed to Git, and it is shared with no one.
editions.limits: A project keeps at most {max} editions, and a book can be up to {mb} MB. This project has {n}. The files count toward the storage of the project and of the person who imported them, as attachments do.
editions.readonly_note: You can read this list. Only owners and editors can download an original file.
editions.chapters_h: Chapters as the book was read
editions.chapters_hint: This is the book as it was read before any change you made while importing. A chapter you left out is marked, and so is one you joined to another.
editions.chapters_more: And {n} more chapters, not listed here.
editions.diff.all_same: Every chapter is the same as the edition's.
editions.diff.compare_note: Both books are read again on the server, one comparison at a time. Nothing is imported or changed. Only editors of both projects can compare, because the text of both books is shown.
editions.diff.confirm_box: I have checked that “{t}” in the edition is the chapter I mean.
editions.diff.guess_h: How the chapters are paired, and what a guess is
editions.diff.guess_a: A guess is a pairing made by comparing the chapters: by their title, by how much of their text they share, or, between two editions, by the same file name. It is a best match and not a record, and it can be wrong, most of all when a chapter was rewritten, renamed or split.
editions.diff.guess_b: Chapters the import recorded are paired from that record and are not guesses. The confidence is a score made from the method and from the text the two chapters share. It is not a probability.
editions.diff.guess_line: Paired by comparing them ({how}), confidence {score}. Check that these are the same chapter.
editions.diff.hidden: {n} more chapters are not listed here.
editions.diff.keep_note: To keep your version, do nothing: nothing changes until you press a button on this page.
editions.diff.legend: Word by word, text struck through and marked − is only in the edition, and text underlined and marked + is only in the project. Both are also said in words, for a screen reader.
editions.diff.legend_compare: Word by word, text struck through and marked − is only in the first edition, and text underlined and marked + is only in the second. Both are also said in words, for a screen reader.
editions.diff.no_changes: The two texts are the same.
editions.diff.no_net: Words are counted as added and as removed, never as a net figure: a cut is not a loss, and a rewrite is not a gain.
editions.diff.partial_d: Some chapters differ but were not compared word by word, so their words are not in the totals. Chapters not compared: {n}.
editions.diff.pick_first: Choose the first, older edition of the two.
editions.diff.pick_intro: Choose the second, later edition. It can be another edition of this project, or one of another project you edit.
editions.diff.pick_none: That project has no edition to compare with.
editions.diff.readers_note: You can see the list of chapters and the counts. The text of each difference is for editors.
editions.diff.take_a: Puts this chapter back as the edition had it: its text becomes the edition's text.
editions.diff.take_b: The text it has now is saved first as a version in the chapter's history, so nothing is lost and you can go back to it. No words are counted toward your goals.
editions.diff.take_h: Put this chapter back as the edition had it
editions.diff.too_different_d: No chapter was compared word by word. The chapters are still listed, paired where the import recorded it.
editions.diff.failed: The comparison could not be made.
editions.diff.gone: That chapter is not in this comparison.
editions.diff.stale: This chapter changed since you opened it. It is shown again as it is now. Check it, then try again.
editions.diff.made: Suggestions made: {n}. They wait in Review, and the text does not change until someone accepts them.
editions.diff.need_confirm: This chapter was paired by a guess. Tick the box to say you have checked it, then try again.
editions.diff.taken_already: The chapter already had exactly the edition's text, so nothing changed.
imp.js.moved_top: Moved {t} to the top level of the book.
imp.js.joined: Joined {t} into {p}. It is listed under Left out of the import, and can be put back.
imp.js.stays: {t} cannot be left out while {j} is joined into it. Put {j} back first.
imp.js.no_join: Choose a chapter to join this one into.
imp.js.join_part: A part, or a chapter with chapters inside it, cannot be joined. Make it a chapter first, or move its chapters.
imp.js.join_none: There is no other chapter to join this into.
imp.js.nest_none: There is no other chapter to nest this under.
editions.chapter.open_joined: Open the document it was joined into
editions.diff.coarse_total: Chapters counted by whole paragraph: {n}. A paragraph in them was too long to compare word by word, so their counts are larger than the real change.
editions.diff.coarse_row: Counted by whole paragraph here: this chapter has a paragraph too long to compare word by word, so these counts are larger than the real change.
editions.diff.suggest_page_one: Suggest the one change on this page
editions.diff.suggest_page_note: Offers the differences on this page, {from} to {to}, and no others. They wait in Review as suggestions, and the text does not change until someone accepts them.
editions.diff.made_page: Suggestions made: {n} of the {total} differences on this page. They wait in Review, and the text does not change until someone accepts them.
editions.diff.page_partial: {reason} Press the button again for the rest of this page.
editions.diff.too_many: A page offers at most 50 differences at a time.
editions.diff.pages_bottom: Pages of differences, end of the list
editions.diff.full_first: The first edition's whole text ({n} words)
editions.diff.full_second: The second edition's whole text ({n} words)
editions.diff.cannot_compare: That project cannot be compared with. Check that you are an editor of it and that it is unlocked.
desktop.window_h: Open Scríobh from its own window
desktop.window_p: This copy of Scríobh belongs to the desktop application and signs in only from the application's own window. A browser tab cannot sign in to it. Open the Scríobh application instead.
desktop.profile_lede: Scríobh keeps one local profile on this computer. Your name appears on what you write and in what you export.
desktop.profile_local: This is a local profile. It has no password and nothing to recover: it is the person at this computer, under this account. Anyone who can use your account on this computer can open your writing.
desktop.profile_name_hint: As you want it shown. You can change it later in Settings.
desktop.profile_email_hint: Only kept on this computer. It is used where you choose to send something by mail; nothing is sent to it now.
desktop.profile_err_name_long: That name is too long: 80 characters at most.
desktop.profile_err_name_invalid: That name has characters that cannot be shown.
desktop.profile_err_email_invalid: That does not look like an email address. Leave it empty if you would rather not give one.
desktop.profile_err_email_long: That email address is too long.
desktop.id_intro: How this copy of Scríobh knows who you are. By default it is the local profile, with no password. An administrator can switch it to an identity provider of your organisation, and back.
desktop.id_saved: The provider's settings are saved. Nothing has changed yet.
desktop.id_verified_line: You signed in at the provider. You can make the switch now.
desktop.id_problem: The last switch was not made: {why}.
desktop.id_pending_external: The switch to the external provider is made when Scríobh next starts. Quit and open it again.
desktop.id_pending_embedded: The switch back to the local profile is made when Scríobh next starts. Quit and open it again.
desktop.id_ext_p: The OpenID Connect provider to sign in through instead of the local profile. Saving changes nothing by itself.
desktop.id_redirect: Register this redirect address at the provider (the port is this computer's; most providers accept any loopback port, and you can fix one below):
desktop.id_issuer_hint: Exactly as the provider's discovery document names it, down to a trailing slash. It must be https.
desktop.id_secret_hint: Kept sealed on this computer and never shown again. Leave it empty for a public client.
desktop.id_secret_kept: A secret is stored. Leave this empty to keep it, or type a new one.
desktop.id_no_secret: This is a public client: store no secret
desktop.id_admin_group_hint: Leave it empty and you stay the administrator. Name a group and the provider decides at every sign-in; you must be in it to make the switch.
desktop.id_groups_hint: Other people who sign in through the provider need one of these groups.
desktop.id_port_hint: For a provider that wants one exact redirect address: Scríobh then uses this port on this computer whenever it signs in through the provider.
desktop.id_switch_p: Your account, with everything in it, moves to your identity at the provider. Nothing is matched by email address: the only account that moves is yours, and only to the identity you prove below. The local profile stops working until you switch back.
desktop.id_step_prove: Sign in at the provider once, to prove the settings work and to show who you are there.
desktop.id_step_switch: Confirm the switch. It is made when Scríobh next starts.
desktop.id_switch_needs: Sign in at the provider first.
desktop.id_confirm_issuer: Type the issuer URL to confirm
desktop.id_back_p: The account that was moved to the provider becomes the local profile again, with everything in it. Other people who signed in through the provider keep their accounts but cannot sign in until you switch again.
desktop.id_confirm_name: Type the local profile's name to confirm
desktop.id_back_go: Go back at the next start
desktop.id_err_unreachable: The provider did not answer, or its issuer URL does not match what it reports. Check the settings and try again.
desktop.id_err_refused: The sign-in at the provider was not completed. Try again.
desktop.id_err_email: The provider did not send a verified email address for you. Scríobh needs one to sign you in, so the switch would lock you out.
desktop.id_err_group: You are not in the administrators' group you named. Making the switch would take administration away from you.
desktop.lm_intro: Scríobh can use a language model that runs on this computer, so nothing you write leaves it. Scríobh does not include a model and never downloads one.
desktop.lm_look_p: Pressing the button makes one request to the Ollama model server on this computer (127.0.0.1, port 11434) and lists the models it has. Nothing is asked until you press it.
desktop.lm_look_go: Look for Ollama on this computer
desktop.lm_not_found: No model server answered on this computer.
desktop.lm_not_found_help: If you want one, install Ollama yourself, start it, fetch a model with it, and look again. Scríobh will not do any of that for you.
desktop.lm_no_models: Ollama is running, but it has no models. Fetch one with Ollama (for example: ollama pull llama3.2), then look again.
desktop.lm_found.one: Ollama is running and has {n} model.
desktop.lm_found.other: Ollama is running and has {n} models.
desktop.lm_added: The provider is added, marked local.
desktop.lm_added_link: Switch AI on and choose where it is used
desktop.lm_err_model: Choose one of the models listed.
desktop.lm_about_h: What this does and does not do
desktop.lm_about_p: Using a model adds an AI provider for this computer's Ollama and marks it local, which keeps its requests on this computer. AI stays off until you switch it on, and each project chooses whether to use it; a project can be set to local providers only.
desktop.lm_about_fine: Scríobh never starts, installs or updates Ollama, and never downloads a model.
desktop.ext_lede: This copy of Scríobh signs in through your organisation's identity provider, and its sign-in page cannot be shown in this window. Open this address in your web browser and sign in there:
desktop.ext_keep: Keep this application open while you work: it is what serves that address. Your writing stays on this computer.
desktop.ext_back: To use this window again, an administrator switches back to the local profile under This computer, in the account menu.
confirm.signout_unsaved: This browser holds unsaved text that was never saved to the server (chapters or notes: {n}). Sign out and discard it?
confirm.signout_locked: This browser holds text of projects that have a passphrase and are locked (projects: {n}), so it cannot be checked against the saved text. Unlock them to save the text first, or sign out and discard it.
desktop.id_browser_p: The provider's sign-in page is another site, which this application's window does not open. Make an address, open it in your web browser, and sign in at the provider there; then come back here.
desktop.id_ticket_note: Open this address in your web browser. It works once, for five minutes, and only records who you are at the provider: it signs nobody in. When the browser says it is done, reload this page.
desktop.id_ticket_bad_p: It was already used, is more than five minutes old, or was not made by this copy of Scríobh. Make a new one on the identity page of the application.
desktop.id_ticket_done_p: Your sign-in at the provider was recorded. Nobody was signed in on this browser. Go back to the application's window, reload the identity page, and confirm the switch there.

studio.forecast.basis: From your last {days} days, in which you counted on {writing} days: about {n} {measure} a day

studio.mail.title: Progress email

studio.ui.title: Writing studio
studio.ui.intro: Your writing, counted on this server and shown to nobody but you. Words you add count; cutting is part of writing and is never held against a day.
studio.ui.welcome: This page fills in as you write. Open a project, write a little, and today's words appear here.
studio.ui.delta.7d.same: The same as the 7 days before
studio.ui.delta.30d.same: The same as the 30 days before
studio.ui.delta.365d.same: The same as the 365 days before
studio.ui.quick_note: Opens {title} and starts a session timer with that target.
studio.ui.cal.caption: Words added each day. One column a week, Monday at the top.
studio.ui.cal.sum.one: 1 writing day in the last {weeks} weeks
studio.ui.cal.sum.other: {n} writing days in the last {weeks} weeks
studio.ui.cal.legend: The four sizes are read from your own writing days: up to {a} words, up to {b}, up to {c}, and more.
studio.ui.cal.legend_uniform: Your writing days so far all hold the same number of words, so they share one size.
studio.ui.cal.hint: Select a day to read its figure. With the calendar focused, the arrow keys move from day to day.
studio.ui.cal.key: A larger square is a day with more words. A ring marks a day a daily goal was met, and a dashed outline marks today. An empty day is simply empty.
studio.ui.goals.empty: A goal is a number you choose: words a day, sessions a week, a manuscript's length. It is yours to change whenever the weeks change.
studio.ui.goals.title: Goals
studio.ui.goals.intro: Daily, weekly and monthly goals, and totals to reach. Goals count words added, never net words, and a day without writing is never counted against one.
studio.ui.goals.archived_intro: Goals you ended. Their record stays, and what was met stays met.
studio.ui.goals.new_intro: One goal for each combination of what is counted, how often, and where.
studio.ui.goals.f_target_h: A whole number, such as 500 words a day or 3 sessions a week.
studio.ui.goals.f_deadline_h: For a total to reach. With a deadline the page estimates a pace and a finishing date.
studio.ui.goals.updated: Goal changed. Periods already over keep the target they had.
studio.ui.goal.net: Net change in this period: {n} words. Cutting never counts against a goal.
studio.ui.goal.on_project: Set on that project's Goals page, and changed there.
studio.ui.goal.change_intro: A change starts a new version from today. Periods already over keep the target they had, and a period already met stays met.
studio.ui.goal.archive_ask: Archive this goal? Its record stays, and it cannot be started again; you can make a new one.
studio.ui.goal.archive_note: Archiving ends a goal and keeps its record.
studio.ui.goal.periods_intro: Each period is read against the target that was in force then.
studio.ui.goal.periods_empty: Nothing yet. The first period is still running.
studio.ui.goal.versions_intro: Every target this goal has had, newest first.
studio.ui.chart.empty: Nothing written in this range yet. The line draws itself as you write.
studio.ui.pace.day.one: Pace: 1 word a day over the whole range
studio.ui.pace.day.other: Pace: {n} words a day over the whole range
studio.ui.pace.writing_day.one: 1 word on a day you wrote
studio.ui.pace.writing_day.other: {n} words on a day you wrote
studio.ui.pace.net: Net change over the range: {n} words
studio.ui.pat.empty: Once there is some writing in this range, your fullest weekday and time of day appear here.
studio.ui.best_hour: Most words in sessions begun between {from} and {to}
studio.ui.pat.note: Times are read from the hour a writing session began, in your own time zone.
studio.ui.trend.fig: {recent} words in the last three weeks, {before} in the three before
studio.ui.proj.note: Your own words. Nobody else's numbers are shown here, and yours are shown to nobody else.
studio.ui.proj.empty: Nothing written this week or last. The projects you write in appear here.
studio.ui.hidden.one: 1 project is locked and not counted.
studio.ui.hidden.other: {n} projects are locked and not counted.
studio.ui.private: Every number here is computed on this server and stays on it unless you make a progress card or turn on the progress email.
studio.ui.sprint.intro: A sprint is a stretch of writing with a clock: choose a length, write, and see what the stretch held.
studio.ui.sprint.none: A sprint runs on a project you can write in. Create one in the library, or ask to be made an editor.
studio.ui.sprint.m0: A session timer with no set end
studio.ui.sprint.hint: Starting opens the project's writing view. The words are counted by the saves the editor already makes.
studio.ui.sprint.abandon_note: Stopping keeps the sprint in your statistics. Setting it aside leaves it out; the words stay in the day either way.
studio.ui.sprints.title: Sprints
studio.ui.sprints.intro: Start a sprint or a session timer, and see what your sprints have held.
studio.ui.sprints.empty: No sprints in this range yet. The first one you finish or stop appears here.
studio.ui.sprints.best.one: Most words in one sprint: 1, on {date} ({minutes} min)
studio.ui.sprints.best.other: Most words in one sprint: {n}, on {date} ({minutes} min)
studio.ui.sprints.note: A sprint that crosses midnight holds the words of both days. A sprint set aside is not listed.
studio.ui.data.title: Compare and export
studio.ui.data.intro: Two periods side by side, and your numbers as files.
studio.ui.compare.p_this_week: This week so far and last week
studio.ui.compare.p_this_month: This month so far and last month
studio.ui.compare.p_last_30: The last 30 days and the 30 before
studio.ui.compare.note: The difference is the first period less the second. It is a number, not a verdict: weeks differ.
studio.compare.so_far.one: The first finished day of each period, so the two sides are the same length. Today is not in it: it is on the Today card
studio.compare.so_far.other: The first {days} finished days of each period, so the two sides are the same length. Today is not in it: it is on the Today card
studio.compare.finished: The finished days of each period: today is not in them, and is on the Today card
studio.compare.starts_tomorrow: No day of this period is finished yet, so there is nothing to set beside the one before. The comparison starts tomorrow.
studio.compare.unequal: The periods are {a} and {b} days long, so no difference is worked out.
studio.ui.compare.own: Compare other dates, or two projects
studio.ui.compare.drafts: Choose a project on each side over the same dates to set two drafts beside each other.
studio.ui.export.intro: Your numbers as a file you keep. Made on this server from your own data; the file names say what and when.
studio.ui.export.table_h: Markdown holds everything in one file and ignores this choice.
studio.ui.export.note: Projects locked in this session are not in a file, as they are not on this page.
studio.ui.card.title: Progress card
studio.ui.card.intro: A private link to a small page with your streak and your goals as numbers. Anyone with the link sees those, and not a word of any project.
studio.ui.card.once_note: Copy it now. It is shown this once and cannot be shown again.
studio.ui.card.once_path: This is the path on this server. Put this server's address in front of it.
studio.ui.card.png_failed: The picture could not be drawn here. The SVG download holds the same card.
studio.ui.card.shows: A card shows your current streak, your longest, how many days you wrote in the past month, and up to three goals as numbers. It never shows a document's title, a comment or any text.
studio.ui.card.label: A note for yourself
studio.ui.card.label_h: Up to 60 characters. Never shown on the card.
studio.ui.card.days_h: From 1 to 365. After that the link opens nothing.
studio.ui.card.projects: Name the project of a goal that is about one project
studio.ui.card.projects_h: Left off, the card says a project goal and names nothing. A project with a passphrase is never named or counted.
studio.ui.card.revoke_ask: Revoke this card? Its link stops working at once.
studio.ui.card.revoked: Card revoked. Its link opens nothing now.
studio.ui.card.public_note: Numbers and their plain words, and nothing of the writing itself.
studio.ui.mail.quiet: Off until you turn it on. Nothing is sent for a week or month with no writing in it.
studio.ui.mail.off_server: Mail is not switched on for this server, so there is nothing to turn on here.
studio.ui.mail.no_email: Your account has no email address from your sign-in provider, so nothing can be sent.
studio.ui.mail.confirm: Your account address changed to {email}, so the progress email stopped. Turn it on again to send it there.
studio.ui.mail.on_weekly: On: each Monday morning, for the week before.
studio.ui.mail.on_monthly: On: on the first of each month, for the month before.
studio.ui.mail.to: It goes to {email}, the address of your account, and nowhere else.
studio.ui.mail.when: It is sent in the morning in your time zone, {zone}.
studio.ui.mail.saved_off: The progress email is off. Nothing will be sent.
studio.ui.nudges.what: Short notes on the dashboard, such as the words to go today or a run of days. At most three a day, never in the writing view.
studio.ui.nudges.label: Show notes on the dashboard
studio.ui.err.range: Give both dates, the first no later than the second, at most ten years apart.
studio.ui.err.compare: Give all four dates, each first date no later than its second, and projects you can open.
studio.ui.err.goal_exists: You already have that goal. Change its target instead.
studio.ui.err.too_many_goals: You have 20 active goals. Archive one to make room.
studio.ui.err.sprint_running: A sprint is already running. Stop it or set it aside first.
studio.ui.err.no_sprint: No sprint is running now. It may have reached its end.
studio.ui.err.too_many_cards: You have five live cards. Revoke one to make another.
studio.ui.err.mail_off: Mail is not switched on for this server.
studio.ui.err.gone: That is no longer there, or its project is locked or in the trash.
studio.ui.err.role: You can read that project but not write in it.
studio.ui.err.archived: This goal is archived. Make a new one to go on.
studio.ui.err.f_target: Enter a whole number of at least 1. A day takes up to 100,000 words.
studio.ui.err.f_deadline: Choose a date from today on, for a total to reach.
studio.ui.err.f_project_id: Choose a project you can open.
studio.ui.err.f_minutes: Choose a length, or enter 1 to 240 minutes.
studio.ui.err.f_expires_days: Enter a number of days from 1 to 365.
studio.ui.err.f_label: A note is up to 60 characters on one line.
studio.js.over: Time is up. Finish your sentence
studio.js.abandoned: Sprint set aside. What you wrote stays
studio.js.running: A sprint is already running. Stop it or set it aside first
studio.js.failed: The sprint could not be started here
studio.ui.pg.intro: Your own words on this project, week by week. Weekly and monthly goals, sessions and sprints live in the Writing Studio.
studio.ui.pg.goal: Add a studio goal for this project
studio.ui.pg.empty: Nothing written here in the last twelve weeks.
